newsitem.title: USA: MGE SPRING WHEAT ENDS WEAK AS CORN SPILLOVER FADES.
newsitem.headline: MGE SPRING WHEAT ENDS WEAK AS CORN SPILLOVER FADES.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures drifted off their earlier highs and settled lower as spillover strength from corn faded, traders said.
U.S. wheat futures markets firmed early on spillover support from CBOT corn, which opened limit-up after USDA's August crop report dramatically cut back its estimate of U.S. corn production.
But wheat began to trade its own fundamentals at the midsession. MGE traders said the crop report was neutral for spring wheat but was somewhat bearish for total U.S. wheat production.
"The thing today was that our spread trade was heavy. That's where we had a lot going on. As far as outright trading goes, it was erratic and thin," a trader said.
MGE spring wheat settled 1-3/4 to 3-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with September down 1-3/4 cents at $3.94-1/4. Earlier, Sept had been as high as $4.02, up six cents on the day.

Traders said Atwood/Peavey bought one million bushels of the December/March spread. Atwood also sold one million Dec. Linnco sold one million Sept and one million Dec. Cargill Investor Services bought 1.4 million Sept, traders said.
The MGE estimated Tuesday's spring wheat futures volume at 25.749 million bushels, up from 13.325 million Monday.
